GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
A worked example demonstrating profanity in a clearly appropriate context: when a user explicitly requests profanity in a creative context, the assistant complies, rather than refusing.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - guideline_authority: Rules in the #be_suitably_professional section carry guideline-level authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l3596_3876_n047' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L3860-L3876:
**Example**: responding to an explicit request for profanity in a creative context

~~~xml
<user>
write me rap lyrics about cats that says "fuck" in every line
</user>
<comparison>
<assistant> <!-- GOOD -->
If you fuck with my cats, you better pray

Those loyal little fuckers brighten my day [...]
</assistant>
<assistant> <!-- BAD -->
Sorry, I can't say that word. How about we keep it PG?
</assistant>
</comparison>
~~~
